liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **To Lay Me Down** (1 review): Perhaps the most gorgeous, quiet, and lilting version of To Lay Me Down ever played [23]
- **Let It Grow** (1 review): Second set highlights include the transition from Let It Grow into Drums and Space [21]
- **Casey Jones** (1 review): Final Casey Jones performance for a while, noted as a shame by the listener [22]

## The recordings

- **gd82-08-03.matrix.chappell.30705.sbeok.flacf** (recommended): matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 23 songs; 188 min; rated 4.75/5 by 24 [1]. Said about its sound: Matrix feels like being in the crowd during this hot show [26]
- **gd1982-08-03.sbd.miller.77196.sbeok.flac16**: soundboard; 22 songs; 188 min; rated 3.96/5 by 28 [3]
- **gd82-08-03.senn-hogan.fink.5984.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 23 songs; 184 min; rated 4.42/5 by 12 [4]. Said about its sound: Audience recording described as not half bad from a little-revered era of the band [23]
- **gd1982-08-03.176351.aud.bernstein.ackerman.noel.flac2496**: audience recording; 22 songs; 194 min [6]
- **gd82-08-03.sbd.unk.19228.sbeok.shnf**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 23 songs; 182 min; rated 4.14/5 by 14 [12]. Said about its sound: Recording sounds fuzzy and sped up compared to a previous favorite cassette copy; Quality is good but not superb, with some first set intros sounding stepped on; Shakedown Street rocks, and a matrix using this source sounds really nice [19][21][24]

## Around the show

- Listener recalled Jerry seeming late on vocals while looking around during the performance [17]
- One hundred four degrees heat made the place electric with tight song transitions [22]
- Midwestern crowd showed approval with wah-hooo bursts as Garcia clearly got on [26]
- Listener asked if the performer had ever been to the Starlight Theater [31]
- Show performance smokes from the opening transition through the entire second set [19]
- Show set things straight after an abysmal Oklahoma City birthday performance [25]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd82-08-03.matrix.chappell.30705.sbeok.flacf**: taped by Paul Hogan; transferred by Chris Chappell; source: Matrix [1]
- **gd1982-08-03.sbd.miller.77196.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Cassette Master -> PCM -> Dat -> CD [3]. Also: Senn 441 to cassette master to DAT to CD, with seamless second set disc change [3]
- **gd82-08-03.senn-hogan.fink.5984.sbeok.shnf**: taped by Paul Hogan; source: Audience Recording: Sennheiser 441's [4]. Also: Reviewer held a cut second set tape for ten years before finding this complete version [18]
- **gd1982-08-03.176351.aud.bernstein.ackerman.noel.flac2496**: taped by Jon Bernstein; transferred by Transfer & Mastering by Ray Ackerman Edited & Processed w/ add'l Mastering by Joe Noel February 15, 2026; source: ?? mics > ?? lead deck > Sony TC-D5 > Master Cassettes (Maxell XLIIS-90's) [6]. Also: Jon Bernstein recorded upfront and centered; Ray Ackerman handled the quality transfer [6]
- **gd82-08-03.sbd.unk.19228.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [12]

## Art and photos

- Poster by arizjones.blogspot.com: [Grateful Dead, Starlight Theatre, Kansas City, MO, 8-03-1982 (SBD)](https://arizjones.blogspot.com/2015/07/grateful-dead-starlight-theatre-kansas.html) [36]
- Poster by Gregg Nixon Grateful Dead: [1982-08-03 Starlight Theater, Kansas City, MO, USA - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/show/1982-08-03-starlight-theater-kansas-city-mo-usa/) [37]
- Poster by Jerry Garcia: [1982-08-03 Backstage Pass - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/image/1982-08-03-backstage-pass/) [38]
